reference.title: Scenario 11 — Three-level deep nested Numbered list in Procedure (Sub-steps and Options)
reference.shortdesc: Consider a procedure where the first two levels represent procedural actions, and the third level

section.p: Consider a procedure where the first two levels represent procedural actions, and the third level presents mutually exclusive options the user must choose from, rather than supporting reference details.

row.entry: [Heading 2]: Configure the Server [List Number, level 0]: Configure the server. [List Number, level 1]: Select the authentication mode. [List Number, level 2]: Local Authentication [List Number, level 2]: LDAP Authentication [List Number, level 2]: SAML Authentication [List Number, level 0]: Restart the service.

entry.codeblock: <task id="configure_the_server"> <title>Configure the Server</title> <taskbody> <steps> <step> <cmd>Configure the server.</cmd> <substeps> <substep> <cmd>Select the authentication mode.</cmd> <choices> <choice>Local Authentication</choice> <choice>LDAP Authentication</choice> <choice>SAML Authentication</choice> </choices> </substep> </substeps> </step> <step> <cmd>Restart the service.</cmd> </step> </steps> </taskbody> </task>

section.p: Result: Level 0 maps to <steps><step><cmd> and Level 1 maps to <substeps><substep><cmd>, same as a standard multi-level procedure. However, because the Level 2 items are short, mutually exclusive labels rather than descriptive supporting detail, the converter maps Level 2 to <choices><choice> instead of <info><ol>.
